public_rationale: In his words, 'Expansion' points back to Microsoft's data center expansion, which he says Microsoft chose to slow sharply. The claim is that this expansion is 'absolutely necessary' for generative AI to keep evolving and growing. That is a counterfactual. It could only be tested if Microsoft actually stopped expanding and we then saw whether generative AI still advanced. Microsoft's own reports show its capital spending stayed very high ($24.2 billion in the quarter ending June 2025) and was guided higher (over $30 billion the next quarter). So the test case never happened. He also gave no period, scale, or measure of 'evolving and expanding'. Swapping in an industry-wide reading would add words he did not say. Even then, industry-wide expansion never stopped, so the claim would remain untested. The claim cannot be graded true or false.
limitations: Grading depends on reading 'Expansion' as Microsoft's expansion. Under either reading, the necessity claim stays untestable.
Evidence is used only as context to show that the test case did not arise.

Here that would mean Microsoft actually stopping or sharply cutting its expansion, and then seeing whether generative AI still advanced. He named no period, scale, or measure of 'evolving and expanding'.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Would need evidence that generative AI kept evolving and growing during a period when Microsoft's data center expansion had in fact stalled or reversed. This cannot be observed either, because Microsoft kept expanding.
